1	import React from 'react';
2	import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
3	import { defineMessages, useIntl } from 'react-intl';
4	import { ZimmProductCardMedia } from '../../molecules/zimmProductCardMedia';
5	import type { ZimmProductCardMediaImage } from '../../molecules/zimmProductCardMedia';
6	import { ZimmProductCardContent } from '../../molecules/zimmProductCardContent';
7	import type { ZimmSizeChipValue } from '../../molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup';
8	
9	/**
10	 * SFCC-236 Step 6 — the organism that assembles Step 4's `ZimmProductCardMedia` and Step 5's
11	 * `ZimmProductCardContent` into the full product card, across the three confirmed variations.
12	 * Figma component set `Product-card`, node `40000223:2822` (20 variants: Size x State x Type x
13	 * Unavailable), file `wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm`. The variation matrix below reflects the resolved
14	 * `hidden`-attribute reading confirmed against the real assembled Card-content instances:
15	 *
16	 *   Home      (40000214:6141 default / 40002163:36593 hover)   — image + name only by default;
17	 *             bag/attributes/size-selector hidden always; a hover-CAPABLE pointer reveals price
18	 *             on hover. Mobile (`40000223:2821`) shows price unconditionally instead — it has no
19	 *             Hover variant at all, so a price hidden "by default, revealed on hover" like the
20	 *             original build shipped would never be revealed there at all (Fix E, found in the
21	 *             full-sweep follow-up audit; confirmed live as a real bug, not just a Figma reading).
22	 *             Arrows appear on hover-capable pointers regardless of variation (Media's own
23	 *             concern, driven purely by image count).
24	 *   PLP/PDP   (40002163:41441 default / 40002163:41459 hover)  — image + name + bag (always) +
25	 *             price by default, no attributes, size-selector hidden; hover hides price and
26	 *             reveals the size-selector in its place; arrows appear.
27	 *   Wishlist  (40002187:58446 default / 40002187:58458 hover)  — image + name + bag (always) +
28	 *             attributes (colour+size) + price by default, size-selector hidden; hover hides
29	 *             price and reveals the size-selector, confirmed identical to PLP's own hover reveal
30	 *             via node `40002187:58460` (the Wishlist hover instance carries no `hidden`
31	 *             attribute on "Size Selector" at all) — this is NOT what the SFCC-236 Jira AC text
32	 *             says (it only mentions the image switch + arrows for Wishlist hover). It shipped
33	 *             matching the design anyway — a judgment call made during implementation, not a
34	 *             conflict that was raised on the ticket or separately ratified.
35	 *
36	 * "Recently Viewed Full History" is not a fourth variation — the AC states it behaves exactly
37	 * like PLP, so callers pass `variation: 'plp'` for it.
38	 *
39	 * Unavailable=True (Fix C, SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit) is confirmed designed for **every**
40	 * variation, not just `plp` — an earlier revision of this paragraph claimed the opposite, before
41	 * the Default+Hover Unavailable instances for `home` (40002163:39981 / :39990) and `wishlist`
42	 * (40002187:58452 / :58464) were actually checked. The confirmed rule, identical across all three:
43	 *   - The PLP/Wishlist size-selector hover-swap is suppressed entirely when unavailable — nothing
44	 *     to pick for an out-of-stock item, so price stays visible on hover instead of being replaced
45	 *     (`hoverHidesPrice`/`hoverRevealsSizeSelector` are both AND-ed with `!isUnavailable` below).
46	 *     Home's own hover-reveals-price behaviour is unaffected — its Unavailable Hover reference
47	 *     still reveals price exactly as the in-stock case does.
48	 *   - "Notify me" is hover-gated on hover-capable devices (hidden by default, revealed on
49	 *     hover/focus-visible, confirmed via every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference) but
50	 *     unconditionally visible on touch (confirmed via the Mobile Unavailable references —
51	 *     Mobile has no Hover variant at all, so whatever they show is the only state a touch
52	 *     pointer ever sees, and all of them show notify-me plainly).
53	 * `isUnavailable` and `onNotifyMe` are threaded through uniformly to `ZimmProductCardContent`
54	 * (the only one of the two composed children with an `isUnavailable` concept at all —
55	 * `ZimmProductCardMedia` has no such prop); this organism does not itself restrict `showNotifyMe`
56	 * to any one variation — a caller that never passes `onNotifyMe` simply gets no notify-me button.
57	 *
58	 * Fix F (full-sweep follow-up audit, after the above was already built and approved): the
59	 * Desktop-only "price stays, notify-me is simply added on hover" behaviour above is NOT what
60	 * Mobile does. Mobile PLP/Wishlist Unavailable (`40002163:41488`, `40002187:58475`) both have
61	 * `Price` `hidden="true"` and only "Notify me" visible — a genuine SWAP, unlike Desktop's additive
62	 * treatment — where Mobile Home Unavailable (`40002163:41204`) keeps price visible alongside
63	 * notify-me, unchanged from Desktop. `sizeSelectorUnavailable` (already computed below for the
64	 * size-chip permanent-hide) drives this too, in zimmProductCard.css.ts, since it is already
65	 * exactly "PLP/Wishlist and unavailable" — the same condition, no new variable needed.
66	 *
67	 * The bag icon also has two Mobile-breakpoint hides, both viewport-width concerns unrelated to
68	 * hover capability (see zimmProductCard.css.ts's own responsive rules, keyed off the same
69	 * `breakpoints` token `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` already uses for its padding steps):
70	 *   - `hideBagOnMobile` — PLP only, unconditional. Figma's Mobile PLP/PDP Card-content instances
71	 *     (`40002163:41479` available / `40002163:41488` unavailable) both have the bag icon's
72	 *     `Icons` frame `hidden="true"` regardless of stock status, where Desktop's own PLP instance
73	 *     leaves it visible.
74	 *   - `hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable` (Fix G, same follow-up audit) — Wishlist only, and only
75	 *     when unavailable. Wishlist's Mobile instance shows the bag when available
76	 *     (`40002187:58470`) and hides it only when unavailable (`40002187:58473`) — narrower than
77	 *     PLP's own unconditional rule, so it needs its own flag rather than reusing
78	 *     `hideBagOnMobile`. `index.tsx` combines both into one `bagHiddenOnMobile` boolean before
79	 *     the recipe ever sees it — the recipe only needs "hide this on mobile for this render", not
80	 *     which of the two reasons applies.
81	 *
82	 * KNOWN GAP: `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s `priority` prop (its LCP eager-load escape hatch) has no
83	 * passthrough here — every card composed via this organism lazy-loads its primary image. Not in
84	 * the given component contract for this step; flagged rather than added silently, since a PLP
85	 * page placing this organism above the fold would want it.
86	 *
87	 * Badge (feature addition, not a "Fix" like the ones above — the underlying design gap was
88	 * genuinely closed, not misread): `ZimmProductCardContent`'s docblock used to claim no Figma
89	 * design existed for SFCC-236's badge AC. It does — the "Tag" overlay, confirmed present and
90	 * pixel-identical on every Size/Type variant checked (nodes 40002163:41442, 40002096:12223,
91	 * 40002187:58447, 40002163:41478, 40004599:89266, 40004638:120485) — it was just nested one
92	 * level deeper (inside "Image Group", i.e. `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s domain) than the first pass
93	 * looked. Per Dani Rivett's scope note on the ticket, the badge shows on PLP and Wishlist (and
94	 * therefore Recently Viewed Full History, which already reuses the `plp` variation) and is
95	 * suppressed on Home — driven by `VARIATION_CONFIG.showBadge` below, the same table-driven
96	 * mechanism as every other variation decision in this file. Figma's own Home node still shows
97	 * the Tag layer un-hidden, contradicting that scope note — treating the confirmed written
98	 * requirement as authoritative over the file's possibly-stale layer visibility here, flagged
99	 * rather than silently picked.
100	 *
101	 * Badge count (confirmed after the above shipped, via a Dev Mode Connect Note on the separate
102	 * "Product Cards" Figma file — QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs, node 3448:35976 — distinct from the
103	 * design-system component-set file cited throughout this docblock): "only 1 product badge will
104	 * show up on these product cards - depending on the configured hierarchy, the highest priority
105	 * badge will be shown," with that priority logic owned by SFCC-225. This confirms `badge?:
106	 * string` (a single value, not a list) is the correct, final shape for this prop — not a
107	 * placeholder pending a possible future move to an array. SFCC-225's own already-merged SCAPI
108	 * hook writes `c_productBadges` as an array sorted by `badgePriorityOrder`, so whatever mapper
109	 * eventually feeds this prop (none exists yet — no page consumes this organism) just needs
110	 * `c_productBadges[0]?.productBadge`, not any re-sorting of its own.
111	 *
112	 * Hover image-swap on Home (same Dani-vs-AC contradiction as the Badge note above, resolved the
113	 * same direction): Dani's comment also says "we don't want the hover action (model photo) on
114	 * the homepage," but the AC update three days later frames the tile-image hover-swap as an
115	 * unconditional Core Component behaviour with no Home exclusion — and the code as first shipped
116	 * followed the AC, passing `swapOnHover` to `ZimmProductCardMedia` unconditionally with no
117	 * variation gate at all. Treated the comment as more authoritative than the AC text here too:
118	 * `VARIATION_CONFIG.showHoverImageSwap` now suppresses the swap for `home` specifically. This
119	 * is unrelated to, and does not affect, Home's own
120	 * `hoverRevealsPrice` — that is a separate mechanism (a style flag consumed by this organism's
121	 * own recipe), not `swapOnHover`.
122	 *
123	 * KNOWN GAP (postbuild doc/traceability audit, comment-only — no behaviour change): both
124	 * quotes above, from Dani's scope note (Jira comment 13880 on SFCC-236), truncate at the same
125	 * point. In full, her instruction is no badge and no hover-image-swap on "the Homepage or on
126	 * the Recently Viewed product carousel" — the Badge note above and this Hover image-swap note
127	 * each only implement and discuss the Homepage half. The Recently Viewed carousel half has no
128	 * code path in this file today: that surface is SFCC-83's rail component, which does not exist
129	 * yet and has no entry in the `ZimmProductCardVariation` union above. A rail caller reaching
130	 * for the closest existing option, `variation: 'plp'`, would get `showBadge: true` and
131	 * `showHoverImageSwap: true` from `VARIATION_CONFIG` — the opposite of what Dani asked for on
132	 * that surface. Whoever builds SFCC-83 needs to either add a dedicated `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry
133	 * for the rail (both flags `false`) or get explicit written confirmation on the ticket that the
134	 * suppression doesn't apply there — not assume `'plp'` already covers it.
135	 */
136	
137	/** Re-exported under this organism's own name so a page-level caller never has to reach into a
138	 *  molecule's type — the shape itself is Media's own `ZimmProductCardMediaImage`, not a
139	 *  redeclaration (a hand-copied duplicate would silently drift from its source). */
140	export type ZimmProductCardImage = ZimmProductCardMediaImage;
141	
142	/** `ZimmProductCardContent`'s own already-derived heading-level type (`'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3'`,
143	 *  itself derived from `ZimmProductName`'s `as` prop) — read via `ComponentProps` off the
144	 *  component this organism actually forwards it to, rather than a hand-typed duplicate union. */
145	type ZimmProductCardHeadingLevel = React.ComponentProps<typeof ZimmProductCardContent>['headingLevel'];
146	
147	/**
148	 * Exported alongside `ZimmProductCardProps` (not just kept module-private) so a test/fixture can
149	 * build a properly *narrowed* per-variation props object — e.g.
150	 * `ZimmProductCardBaseProps & ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation` — instead of a value typed as the
151	 * full union. This matters for real, not just for convenience: TypeScript's excess-property
152	 * check on a *union* target is weak (a property valid on any one member is not flagged as excess
153	 * on a fresh literal discriminated toward a different member), so proving "the wishlist-only
154	 * fields don't exist on Home" needs an assignment to Home's own narrow shape specifically, not to
155	 * the union alias — see index.test.tsx's `@ts-expect-error` cases and its overloaded
156	 * `buildCardProps` helper.
157	 */
158	export type ZimmProductCardBaseProps = {
159	  /** Stable per-card identifier. Not used for any layout/behavioural decision — exposed as a
160	   *  `data-product-id` attribute on the root element as a DOM hook for QA automation/analytics,
161	   *  the same kind of caller-facing marker `data-testid` already serves in this build's other
162	   *  components, without overloading that attribute's own testing-only convention. */
163	  id: string;
164	  /** PDP destination, pre-site-prefixed by the caller — forwarded straight to
165	   *  `ZimmProductCardContent`'s own `href` (see that component's own JSDoc on trust level). */
166	  href: string;
167	  name: string;
168	  headingLevel: ZimmProductCardHeadingLevel;
169	  primaryImage: ZimmProductCardImage;
170	  hoverImage?: ZimmProductCardImage;
171	  images?: ZimmProductCardImage[];
172	  currentPrice?: string;
173	  originalPrice?: string;
174	  isPriceLoading?: boolean;
175	  isUnavailable?: boolean;
176	  /** Only meaningful when `isUnavailable` is true. See the module docblock for why this is not
177	   *  restricted to the `plp` variation at the type level. */
178	  onNotifyMe?: () => void;
179	  /**
180	   * Merchandiser-configured badge label (e.g. "Runway", "Exclusive"). Always a single value —
181	   * confirmed via a Figma Dev Mode Connect Note that only the single highest-priority badge is
182	   * ever shown, never a list (see the module docblock's "Badge count" note). Not restricted to
183	   * any variation at the type level, same reasoning as `onNotifyMe` above — whether it actually
184	   * renders is `VARIATION_CONFIG.showBadge`'s job (PLP/Wishlist show it, Home suppresses it; see
185	   * the module docblock's "Badge" note).
186	   */
187	  badge?: string;
188	};
189	
190	export type ZimmProductCardPlpVariation = {
191	  variation: 'plp';
192	  onAddToBag?: () => void;
193	  sizeChipValues?: ZimmSizeChipValue[];
194	  selectedSizeChipValue?: string;
195	  onSizeChipSelect?: (value: string) => void;
196	};
197	
198	export type ZimmProductCardHomeVariation = {
199	  variation: 'home';
200	  // No additions — Home never shows the bag, attributes, or size chips (see VARIATION_CONFIG).
201	};
202	
203	export type ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation = {
204	  variation: 'wishlist';
205	  /** Required, not optional — the Wishlist AC always shows the attributes line. */
206	  colour: string;
207	  size: string;
208	  /** Required — a wishlist card with no way to remove itself is a spec violation. */
209	  onRemove: () => void;
210	  /** Bag is always visible for Wishlist per the confirmed matrix above. */
211	  onAddToBag?: () => void;
212	  /** Same trio `ZimmProductCardPlpVariation` declares, and for the same reason: confirmed via the
213	   *  real Figma Wishlist Hover instance (node 40002187:58458) during the SFCC-236 Step 6 visual
214	   *  audit that Wishlist's hover reveal is a genuine, populated size-selector swap identical to
215	   *  PLP's — not a PLP-only affordance. `index.tsx`'s render body already forwarded these
216	   *  unconditionally to `ZimmProductCardContent` for every variation (via the
217	   *  `ZimmProductCardVariationFields` cast below); this type previously just didn't expose them
218	   *  to a Wishlist caller, which is what let the Wishlist story ship without ever populating them. */
219	  sizeChipValues?: ZimmSizeChipValue[];
220	  selectedSizeChipValue?: string;
221	  onSizeChipSelect?: (value: string) => void;
222	};
223	
224	export type ZimmProductCardProps = ZimmProductCardBaseProps &
225	  (ZimmProductCardPlpVariation | ZimmProductCardHomeVariation | ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation);
226	
227	type ZimmProductCardVariation =
228	  | ZimmProductCardPlpVariation['variation']
229	  | ZimmProductCardHomeVariation['variation']
230	  | ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation['variation'];
231	
232	/**
233	 * Widened, not narrowed: every variation-specific field is optional here regardless of which
234	 * branch is actually active, purely so the component body below can destructure once with no
235	 * `if`/`switch` on `props.variation` — the extensibility AC requires every layout/visibility
236	 * decision to come from `VARIATION_CONFIG`, keyed by the discriminant, never a branching
237	 * statement. The exported `ZimmProductCardProps` discriminated union above is what actually
238	 * enforces correct usage at every call site (proven by the `@ts-expect-error` cases in
239	 * index.test.tsx) — this cast only relaxes internal access inside this file; it changes nothing
240	 * about what a caller may legally pass in.
241	 */
242	type ZimmProductCardVariationFields = Partial<
243	  Omit<ZimmProductCardPlpVariation, 'variation'> &
244	    Omit<ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation, 'variation'> &
245	    Omit<ZimmProductCardHomeVariation, 'variation'>
246	>;
247	
248	type ZimmProductCardVariationConfig = {
249	  showBag: boolean;
250	  showAttributes: boolean;
251	  showSizeChips: boolean;
252	  /** PLP/Wishlist: price is visible by default and hides on hover. */
253	  hoverHidesPrice: boolean;
254	  /** Home only: price is hidden by default and reveals on hover. */
255	  hoverRevealsPrice: boolean;
256	  /** PLP/Wishlist: the size-chip picker is hidden by default and reveals on hover. */
257	  hoverRevealsSizeSelector: boolean;
258	  showRemove: boolean;
259	  /** PLP only (found during the SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit): Figma's Mobile Card-content
260	   *  instance has the bag icon's `Icons` frame `hidden="true"`, unlike Desktop and unlike
261	   *  Wishlist's own Mobile instance (bag stays visible there on every breakpoint). A viewport-
262	   *  width concern, not a hover one — see zimmProductCard.css.ts's own responsive rule. */
263	  hideBagOnMobile: boolean;
264	  /** Wishlist only (found during the follow-up full-sweep visual audit against every variant x
265	   *  state node): unlike PLP's unconditional `hideBagOnMobile`, Wishlist's Mobile Card-content
266	   *  instance shows the bag icon when available (`40002187:58470`) and hides it
267	   *  (`Icons` frame `hidden="true"`) only when unavailable (`40002187:58473`) — narrower than
268	   *  `hideBagOnMobile`, and combined with it (not replacing it) in the `bagHiddenOnMobile`
269	   *  derivation below, since the two are mutually exclusive per variation today but there is no
270	   *  reason to assume that stays true forever. */
271	  hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: boolean;
272	  /** Shown on PLP/Wishlist, suppressed on Home — see the module docblock's "Badge" note. */
273	  showBadge: boolean;
274	  /**
275	   * Allows `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s primary/hover image crossfade for this variation. Suppressed
276	   * on Home per Dani Rivett's scope note, overriding the AC's unconditional framing — see the
277	   * module docblock's "Hover image-swap on Home" note. `false` here means a supplied
278	   * `hoverImage` is simply never swapped to, regardless of pointer capability.
279	   */
280	  showHoverImageSwap: boolean;
281	};
282	
283	/**
284	 * The extensibility AC's actual mechanism: every layout/visibility decision this organism makes
285	 * reads from this table, keyed by `variation` — adding a future variation means adding a union
286	 * member above and one row here, touching no JSX. `index.tsx`'s render body contains no
287	 * `switch`/`if` on `props.variation` anywhere (verify with
288	 * `grep -n 'variation ===\|switch (variation)' index.tsx` — zero hits).
289	 */
290	const VARIATION_CONFIG: Record<ZimmProductCardVariation, ZimmProductCardVariationConfig> = {
291	  home: {
292	    showBag: false,
293	    showAttributes: false,
294	    showSizeChips: false,
295	    hoverHidesPrice: false,
296	    hoverRevealsPrice: true,
297	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: false,
298	    showRemove: false,
299	    hideBagOnMobile: false,
300	    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: false,
301	    showBadge: false,
302	    showHoverImageSwap: false,
303	  },
304	  plp: {
305	    showBag: true,
306	    showAttributes: false,
307	    showSizeChips: true,
308	    hoverHidesPrice: true,
309	    hoverRevealsPrice: false,
310	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: true,
311	    showRemove: false,
312	    hideBagOnMobile: true,
313	    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: false,
314	    showBadge: true,
315	    showHoverImageSwap: true,
316	  },
317	  wishlist: {
318	    showBag: true,
319	    showAttributes: true,
320	    showSizeChips: true,
321	    hoverHidesPrice: true,
322	    hoverRevealsPrice: false,
323	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: true,
324	    showRemove: true,
325	    hideBagOnMobile: false,
326	    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: true,
327	    showBadge: true,
328	    showHoverImageSwap: true,
329	  },
330	};
331	
332	const messages = defineMessages({
333	  // Interpolated with the product name, matching ZimmProductPrice's WAS/NOW pattern — Media's
334	  // own `removeLabel` prop is a plain string, so the interpolation happens here, at the one call
335	  // site that actually knows the product name.
336	  removeFromWishlist: {
337	    id: 'product_card.remove.from_wishlist',
338	    defaultMessage: 'Remove {name} from wishlist',
339	  },
340	});
341	
342	const ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_RECIPE = 'ZimmProductCard';
343	
344	/**
345	 * Organism — the full product card, composing `ZimmProductCardMedia` and `ZimmProductCardContent`
346	 * across the `home` / `plp` / `wishlist` variations. See the module docblock above for the
347	 * confirmed Figma variation matrix and this component's own recipe (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`) for
348	 * the stretched-link and hover-reveal mechanics that live entirely in CSS, not in this render
349	 * body — both children are always rendered in full, with every one of their own sub-parts; CSS
350	 * alone decides what is visible for a given variation and pointer capability.
351	 *
352	 * @param props see `ZimmProductCardProps` — a discriminated union on `variation`.
353	 */
354	export const ZimmProductCard = (props: ZimmProductCardProps) => {
355	  const {
356	    id,
357	    href,
358	    name,
359	    headingLevel,
360	    primaryImage,
361	    hoverImage,
362	    images,
363	    currentPrice,
364	    originalPrice,
365	    isPriceLoading,
366	    isUnavailable,
367	    onNotifyMe,
368	    badge,
369	    variation,
370	  } = props;
371	
372	  const { onAddToBag, sizeChipValues, selectedSizeChipValue, onSizeChipSelect, colour, size, onRemove } =
373	    props as ZimmProductCardVariationFields;
374	
375	  const intl = useIntl();
376	  const config = VARIATION_CONFIG[variation];
377	
378	  // Both conditions required — an organism that sets isUnavailable without a real callback
379	  // should not show a dead notify-me button. Mirrors ZimmProductCardContent's own
380	  // showNotifyMeButton co-requirement.
381	  const showNotifyMe = Boolean(isUnavailable) && Boolean(onNotifyMe);
382	
383	  // Fix C (SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit): confirmed against the real Figma Default+Hover
384	  // instances for every variation × Unavailable=True (including the Mobile/no-hover variants,
385	  // which show the only state a touch pointer ever sees) that `isUnavailable` suppresses the
386	  // size-selector hover-swap entirely — there is nothing to pick for an out-of-stock item, so
387	  // price stays visible on hover instead of being replaced. Home's own hover-reveals-price
388	  // behaviour is untouched by this — Home's Unavailable Hover reference (node 40002163:39990)
389	  // still reveals price on hover exactly as the in-stock case does; only the PLP/Wishlist
390	  // hide-and-swap needs suppressing.
391	  //
392	  // Suppressing `hoverRevealsSizeSelector` alone is not enough to reproduce that reference: it
393	  // only stops the organism adding its OWN hide/reveal pair, which leaves the size-chip wrapper
394	  // at Content's own natural (visible) default — briefly shipped that way mid-fix and caught by
395	  // re-checking the real Storybook render against Figma, which confirms size chips stay hidden
396	  // in BOTH states when unavailable, not just "not swapped in on hover". `sizeSelectorUnavailable`
397	  // carries that permanent hide separately, unconditional (not gated by hover-capability at all —
398	  // this isn't a pointer-type concern, unlike everything else in this recipe).
399	  //
400	  // Follow-up (full-sweep visual audit against every variant x state node, not just the sampled
401	  // set the first pass checked): `sizeSelectorUnavailable` ALSO drives a mobile-only price hide
402	  // in the recipe now (Fix F) — confirmed via `get_metadata` that Mobile PLP/Wishlist Unavailable
403	  // hide price and show notify-me in its place (`40002163:41488`, `40002187:58475`), the OPPOSITE
404	  // of Desktop's additive treatment (price stays, notify-me is simply added on hover). Nothing
405	  // extra is computed here for it — the recipe reads the same `sizeSelectorUnavailable` boolean
406	  // for both the size-chip permanent-hide and this new price rule, since both only ever apply to
407	  // the same PLP/Wishlist-and-unavailable case.
408	  const hoverHidesPrice = config.hoverHidesPrice && !isUnavailable;
409	  const hoverRevealsSizeSelector = config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && !isUnavailable;
410	  const sizeSelectorUnavailable = config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && Boolean(isUnavailable);
411	
412	  // Fix G (same follow-up audit): Wishlist-only. `hideBagOnMobile` alone only covers PLP's own
413	  // unconditional mobile hide; Wishlist's bag stays visible on mobile UNLESS unavailable
414	  // (`40002187:58470` vs `40002187:58473`). Combined into one boolean here rather than exposing
415	  // both conditions to the recipe — it only needs to know "hide this on mobile for this render",
416	  // not why.

6	 * more than one populated colour) the row of ZimmColourSwatch rectangles beneath it. This recipe

8	 * ZimmColourSwatch atom's own recipe.

18	 *   - `label` — the label row ("labelContainer" in Figma): the label-group (the two
19	 *     "Colour:"/name text pieces — laid out via a plain Chakra-prop wrapper in the component

24	 *     part, unlike the static "Colour:" piece beside it, because it alone carries the
25	 *     Figma-mandated truncation behaviour: "If Label/Colour name is longer, use truncation"
26	 *     (this node's own interaction annotation).

28	 *     (`isPaginated`), reserves a fixed page-width footprint regardless of how many items the
29	 *     current window actually renders — see its own baseStyle comment below for the layout bug

32	 *   - `pageButton` — each individual chevron button (24x24, holding a 16px ZimmIcon).

40	 * expression below.

43	
44	/**
45	 * The reserved 4-swatch-wide footprint: PAGE_SIZE swatches at the atom's own fixed 47px width
46	 * (see `swatch.width` in zimmColourSwatch.css.ts), with no per-swatch gap
47	 * (`swatches.gap` below is 0, same as the atom's own adjacency). Two consumers share this one

123	      // element. That circular relationship meant the *rendered* width tracked how many items the

144	      alignItems: 'center',
145	      // No inter-button gap value exists in the Figma export handed to this step — left at the

153	      justifyContent: 'center',

# CSS & Styling Conventions

Chakra UI and `.scss` conventions. See [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Rules > Styling for the
higher-level policy (Chakra props first, `.scss` only when insufficient, theme file
ownership/tiers) — this file covers the concrete day-to-day rules underneath that policy.

---

## Tokens — no hardcoded design values

Chakra UI props must use the Chakra token system — no hardcoded hex colours, no pixel
values for spacing, no raw font sizes. Tokens belong in
[overrides/app/theme/foundation/](../../overrides/app/theme/) (Tier 1 — see
[frozenFiles.md](./frozenFiles.md)).

```tsx
// ❌ hardcoded
<Box color="#1A1A1A" padding="16px" />

// ❌ a bare Chakra/theme token string — resolves correctly (theme.colors/theme.space ARE
// registered from the Zimmermann foundations) but is still not allowed in an override
// component; see overrideStyling.md's hierarchy point 2 for why
<Box color="text.default" padding="m" />

// ✅ token, as a raw var(--zimm-*) reference
<Box color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)" padding="var(--zimm-scale-m)" />
```

Type is its own case, not shown above — set it with `textStyle` (`textStyle="body2"`), never
a raw `fontSize`, per [overrideStyling.md](./overrideStyling.md) point 1. There's no
`var(--zimm-*)` substitute for the composite `textStyle` expansion itself, only for its
individual pieces (`var(--zimm-font-size-*)` etc.), so `textStyle` stays a bare key —
it's the one entry in the hierarchy that isn't a colour/spacing token.

**The raw-hex/px/rem/em half of this has a script but no CI gate yet.**
`npm run audit:tokens` (`scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`) scans `overrides/app/components/**`
and `overrides/app/theme/components/**` for exactly this — see
[overrideStyling.md](./overrideStyling.md)'s `Never` note for the full scope and its
acknowledged-exception rules. It's not wired into CI (no `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/` rule
either), so nothing blocks a merge that skips running it — that's still a real gap, just not
an unstarted one.
The bare-token-vs-`var(--zimm-*)` half above **is** mechanically enforced for recipe files —
see `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`, which runs on every `npm run test` — though it
can't see the same mistake made as a JSX/`sx` prop; that half still relies on review.

---

## `.scss` — only when Chakra props are insufficient

Per AGENTS.md, reach for a `.scss` file alongside a component only when Chakra's prop system
genuinely can't express what's needed (e.g. complex pseudo-selectors, keyframe animations,
print styles). When you do:

- **File naming:** matches the component file exactly — `productTile.scss` next to
  `productTile/index.tsx` (see [conventions.md](./conventions.md) > File naming and folder
  structure for the folder layout this sits in).
- **Scoped, co-located only.** No global stylesheets outside `overrides/app/theme/` — a
  component's `.scss` file must only affect that component's own markup.
- **Nesting depth ≤ 3 levels.** Beyond that, the selector is almost always reaching into a
  child component's internals rather than styling its own root — a sign the styling belongs
  in that child instead, or that Chakra's `sx` prop / a theme variant would express it more
  directly.
- **No ID selectors.** Class-based only — an ID selector's specificity makes it
  disproportionately hard to override later (including by a legitimate future Chakra
  variant), and IDs aren't guaranteed unique when a component renders more than once on a
  page.
- **No `!important`** without an inline comment explaining why the override is genuinely
  unavoidable (e.g. fighting a third-party widget's inline styles) — same reasoning as the
  `any`/non-null-assertion escape hatches in [typescript.md](./typescript.md): allowed, but
  the reason has to be visible at the point of use, not left for the next reader to guess.
- **Prefer Chakra's `sx` prop or a theme variant extension over a new `.scss` file** for
  anything that's really just "a Chakra style the prop system doesn't have a named prop for"
  — a new global class is a bigger footprint than a one-off `sx` override, and `sx` keeps the
  style co-located with the JSX that uses it instead of a separate file to keep in sync.

# Design: Fixing the AT-inaccessible / stateful-tab-order hover reveals in `ZimmProductCard`

## Grounding confirmed from the code

Reading the five sites in `zimmProductCard.css.ts` (lines 284-385) plus `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s `carousel` part (172-195) confirms the mechanism exactly as described, with one structural fact that matters a lot for the fix: **every one of the five reveals is currently expressed as a `display: 'none'` (or, for `carousel`, `display:'none'` living in a different file) toggled to `display: 'block'|'flex'`** by `&:hover` / `&:has(:focus-visible)` on the shared card root. `display: none` is the actual defect surface — it is the one CSS property that unconditionally strips an element from the accessibility tree, not just from paint.

Three things I confirmed that materially shape the design:

1. **`ZimmSizeChipGroup`/`ZimmSizeChip` already implement a correct roving-tabindex radiogroup** (`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup/index.tsx:154`, `atoms/zimmSizeChip/index.tsx:44` — `tabIndex={isFocusable ? 0 : -1}`), entirely independent of the wrapper's own hide/reveal styling. Any fix only needs to touch the *wrapper's* visibility mechanism, never the chip-level focus logic.
2. **This exact class of fix already has a working, tested precedent in this codebase**: `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`'s off-page swatches (`molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:205-230`) are kept permanently in the DOM and use `position: 'absolute'` + `clipPath: 'inset(50%)'` (not `display:none`) specifically so "screen readers can navigate the full set and `aria-posinset`/`aria-setsize` reports the correct total count" (index.tsx's own comment, corroborated by `index.stories.tsx:121` and `index.test.tsx:135`). This is the established, already-proven "keep in the a11y tree, paint nothing" technique in this repo — not something I'd be introducing novel.
3. **`zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` deliberately declares no `position`/`display` at all** for `priceWrapper`, `sizeChipWrapper`, `notifyMeButton` (confirmed by reading the file — its own comment at line 179-183 says setting anything there "would fight whatever the organism's hover-reveal CSS tries to do"). So the *entire* hide/reveal mechanism for those three lives in the organism's recipe today, and a fix can stay contained there too — it doesn't need to touch `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`.
4. This repo already has scaffolded-but-empty Playwright a11y projects (`playwright.config.js:69-78`: `a11y-mobile` → `e2e/tests/a11y/mobile`, `a11y-desktop` → `e2e/tests/a11y/desktop`), both Chromium-only (no WebKit project exists), and no axe-core dependency in `package.json`. That's directly relevant to what "verification" can realistically mean here.

## The core design insight

`:focus-visible` (and by extension `:has(:focus-visible)`) is a **heuristic the platform runs to decide whether to *paint* a focus ring**. It was never designed as, and cannot be relied on as, a proxy for "is this element reachable/operable by assistive technology." Theory 1 exists because the CSS in this file is using that heuristic to decide something much bigger than a focus ring — whether the element exists in the accessibility tree at all. Those are two different questions, and conflating them is the actual bug, independent of which selector (`:focus-within` vs `:has(:focus-visible)`) is used to answer it. `983bddf` correctly fixed a *paint-timing* bug (stuck-open ring) using exactly the right tool for that job; it just happened to be reusing the same selector that also gates AT-tree presence, which is a separate concern that needs a separate fix.

That reframing is what makes the primary approach fall out cleanly: **stop using `display` for the "hidden" state. Use it only for things that should never exist for anyone (e.g. the permanent, non-hover-capable-device `sizeChips`/`price` hides that stay outside `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` — those are untouched, correct, and out of scope). For the five interaction-gated reveals, keep the element permanently in the DOM, focusable, and in the accessibility tree, and let `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` toggle only the paint layer** (`position` + `clip-path`, the same two properties `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` already uses).

---

## Approach 1 (Recommended, primary): CSS-only — keep every target present/focusable/AT-exposed; `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` toggles paint only

### Mechanism
For each of the five reveal sites, replace the `display: 'none'` ⟷ `display: 'block'|'flex'` pair with:
- **Hidden (default) state:** `position: 'absolute'`, `clipPath: 'inset(50%)'` — takes the element out of normal flow (so siblings don't reflow around a phantom gap, exactly as `display:none` did) and paints nothing, while the element remains in the DOM, remains focusable, and remains in the accessibility tree.
- **Revealed state** (same `&:hover [...]` / `&:has(:focus-visible) [...]` selectors, byte-for-byte unchanged): `position: 'static'`, `clipPath: 'none'` — restores normal flow and paint.

This requires **zero change to the trigger selectors** — `:hover` and `:has(:focus-visible)` still gate exactly the same thing they gate today (whether the "revealed" declaration block wins the cascade against the "hidden" one). Only the *property values* inside those already-existing blocks change. Because the cascade mechanics are unchanged (same specificity delta between the plain descendant selector and the `&:hover`/`&:has()` compound selector that already reliably overrides it today for `display`), this carries over identically for `position`/`clip-path`.

**Carousel arrow buttons need one extra piece.** `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s `carousel` part sets `pointerEvents: 'none'` on the wrapper (deliberately, so clicks in the empty centre pass through to the image) and re-enables `pointerEvents: 'auto'` on each `arrowButton` individually (lines 194, 207). Once the wrapper is no longer `display:none`, those buttons become real, always-hit-testable elements unless something also constrains their pointer-events. `clip-path` does suppress hit-testing over the clipped region in evergreen engines (this is what the swatch-group precedent already silently depends on — its off-page swatches would produce visible misclicks otherwise, and none are reported), but the carousel case is structurally different (an ancestor explicitly re-enabling `pointer-events` on children), so I'd add an explicit belt-and-braces rule at the organism level — `[data-card-slot="carousel"] button` gets `pointerEvents: 'none'` by default and `pointerEvents: 'auto'` in the two revealed selectors — removing any dependency on clip-path's hit-testing behavior being airtight across every target browser/version. `priceWrapper`/`sizeChipWrapper`/`notifyMeButton` have no such ancestor/child pointer-events split (confirmed by reading `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` in full — none of the three declares `pointerEvents` at all), so they don't need this extra rule.

### Why this resolves both theories, and doesn't reintroduce the mouse bug
- **Theory 1 (AT-inaccessibility):** the control is in the accessibility tree and independently focusable *unconditionally* — whether `:has(:focus-visible)` ever matches for a given VoiceOver-driven focus event becomes irrelevant to whether the control exists for AT at all; it only decides whether it's also *painted*. A VO user who never triggers the heuristic still lands on a real, announced, activatable control via VO's own navigation (VO+Arrow/rotor), because `clip-path`-based hiding — unlike `display:none`/`visibility:hidden` — is defined and already relied on in this exact codebase to keep something in the accessibility tree.
- **Theory 2 (stateful tab order):** since these elements are never removed from the tab order, the *set* of Tab stops in the card is now fixed by DOM structure alone, exactly as the prompt asked. Shift+Tab entering from after the card lands on the true last DOM element (notify-me, or the roving-tabindex size chip, or the last arrow button) rather than skipping to the bag button — no more "reverse direction to reach them."
- **No reintroduction of the `983bddf` stuck-open bug:** that bug was entirely about *when* `:has(:focus-visible)` matches (a click-focused button not un-matching on mouseout until focus moved elsewhere) — a selector-matching-timing question, completely orthogonal to which property the matched rule sets. The selector logic isn't touched, so the same mouse-click-then-mouseout sequence still correctly stops matching `:has(:focus-visible)` at the same moment it does today, and the control reverts to its clipped/paint-inert state identically. One second-order nuance worth flagging honestly: because the element is no longer `display:none`'d, the browser no longer force-blurs it (today, an element becoming `display:none` while focused causes the browser to move focus away; under this approach that forced blur no longer happens). This is harmless — a mouse user never perceives an invisible element quietly retaining `document.activeElement`, and the *next* Tab press simply continues from wherever it silently sat, landing on the next DOM-order stop exactly as ordinary keyboard/focus behavior would predict. It is not a new "stuck" state in any user-visible sense.
- **No "landed on an invisible control" confusion for sighted keyboard users:** the reveal-on-`:focus-visible` mechanism is unchanged and fires in the same paint frame as the focus event (same as `:hover` today) — there is no frame in which a sighted keyboard user's Tab focus sits on a genuinely clipped control. This is identical to today's forward-Tab experience (already confirmed fine per the investigation) and additionally fixes the Shift+Tab-from-after case the same way.
- **Honors the organism's stated design principle exactly, not a deviation from it:** "CSS ALONE decides what is visible — no JS-tracked reveal state" (`index.tsx:349-350`) remains completely true — no JS state is introduced anywhere. Only *which* CSS property expresses visibility changes.

## Appendix: Approach 2 (JS-tracked hover/focus state) — considered, not recommended

### What it would concretely look like
A small piece of state on the organism root (either React `useState` or a plain ref-driven class/data-attribute toggle, to avoid a render on every mouse move): `isHovering` set by real `mouseenter`/`mouseleave` listeners on the root, and `isFocusWithin` set by `focusin`/`focusout` listeners (native events, since they bubble, unlike React's non-capturing `onFocus`/`onBlur`). The reveal condition becomes `isHovering || isFocusWithin`, expressed as a class/data-attribute the CSS then keys off instead of `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)`. To avoid `983bddf`'s stuck-open bug, this would need its own modality distinction — e.g. flagging a `focusin` as "not keyboard-like" when immediately preceded by a `pointerdown`/`mousedown` — which is exactly the logic the well-known `focus-visible` polyfill implements.

### Why it's rejected as the primary path
The reason this doesn't help is structural, not an implementation detail: **there is no signal exposed to page-level JavaScript, any more than to CSS, that says "this focus event was AT-originated."** A hand-rolled `pointerdown`-before-`focusin` heuristic has exactly the same blind spot as the native `:focus-visible` heuristic it would be reimplementing — both are inferring "keyboard-like" from the same limited set of observable DOM events, and VoiceOver's own focus-moving gestures don't produce an observably-different signal to either layer. Reimplementing the heuristic in JS doesn't make it more accurate for the VoiceOver case; it just moves the same imperfect heuristic from the browser engine into application code, with real added costs and no added correctness:
- **Breaks the organism's own explicit design principle** ("CSS alone decides what is visible... no JS-tracked reveal state today," `index.tsx:349-350`) for no accessibility gain.
- **Introduces SSR/hydration-mismatch risk** that pure CSS structurally cannot have — `zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx`'s own docblock (104-107) already states the current CSS-only design deliberately avoids this ("matching the 'keep in DOM, hide via CSS' precedent... so server and client render identically").
- **Adds listener lifecycle/cleanup surface** (mouseenter/leave, focusin/out, plus whatever modality heuristic) for a problem CSS already solves once the underlying "don't gate AT-tree presence behind any interaction heuristic" insight is applied.

The only way a JS approach would actually fix Theory 1 is if it *also* stopped trying to detect modality for the purpose of AT-tree presence and instead adopted the same "always operable, toggle paint only" idea Approach 1 already implements — at which point it is strictly more code and more risk for an identical outcome. There's no version of "JS-based" that beats Approach 1 on the merits; it's included here only because the brief explicitly asked for the comparison to be made concrete rather than dismissed by assertion.

## Recommendation

**Approach 1** (CSS-only: keep every reveal target permanently present/focusable/AT-exposed; `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` toggles only `position`+`clip-path`, mirroring `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`'s already-proven off-page-swatch pattern, plus an explicit `pointer-events` toggle for the carousel's button/wrapper split) is the primary, recommended path. It resolves both theories, requires no new trigger-selector logic (so it cannot reintroduce the `983bddf` mouse bug), fully honors the organism's existing "CSS alone" design principle, and reuses an already-shipped, already-tested pattern from this exact codebase rather than inventing a new mechanism.
